subject: Post-demo: model-fit qualification, parity thresholds, and next steps

Cc: priyom_das@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 18 Apr 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: model-fit qualification, parity thresholds, and next steps

Thanks again for the time today, Daniel — appreciate the candid walkthrough of ClearWave's reconciliation flows and the API call transcripts you shared. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum going.

High-level summary
- Goal: validate whether an open-model candidate can meet or exceed your current in-house baseline on the three core tasks we discussed: intent classification (routing), entity extraction (account identifiers / amounts), and answer-generation quality for customer-facing explanations.
- Success criteria (initial):
  - Intent classification micro-F1 >= 0.86
  - Entity extraction precision >= 0.90 and recall >= 0.85 on masked transaction examples
  - Answer-generation hallucination rate <= 2% per 10k tokens (measured via our hallucination test-suite)
  - End-to-end 95th percentile latency <= 450ms for 512-token sequences under trial batching profile

Recommended open-model candidates to validate (shortlist)
- Redwood-open-2.7B-q4 (quantized) — best latency/cost tradeoff; likely requires prompt engineering for hallucination control
- Falcon-40B-Instruct (baseline comparison) — high-quality generation, expect higher tokens cost and latency; useful as a quality ceiling
- Llama3-13B-rt — balanced middle ground for entity extraction accuracy in our early trials

Benchmarks and artifacts I'm attaching/including:
- prompt_bundle_v1.txt (attached) — recommended prompt templates and contextualization patterns for reconciliation tasks
- benchmark_sample_results.csv (attached) — sample of our benchmark harness run on anonymized ClearWave transcripts (small subset)
- MutualActionPlan-ClearWave.docx (attached) — draft timeline, responsibilities, and trial success gates
- Drive folder with test harness and data: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-example-benchmarks

Quality/regression concerns we flagged during the demo
- Numeric normalization edge cases (leading zeros, currency symbols) triggered entity recall drops in one batch — will add targeted synthetic cases to the trial dataset.
- Prompt-sensitivity: short prompts plus long context produced more concise answers but slightly higher hallucination — propose adding a prompt-robustness gate in the acceptance criteria.

Trial plan (proposed)
- 2-week sandbox: we run three model variants against a canned 10k-sample transcript set you approved.
- Day 3: mid-trial checkpoint with preliminary metrics and prompt tweaks.
- Day 10: full regression run and side-by-side parity report vs your baseline.
- Deliverable: parity report + recommended model & configuration for pilot.

Asks / next steps
1) Please confirm the anonymized dataset we discussed is good for an initial 10k-sample trial (or let us know timing to provision).
2) Can you share a point person for procurement/contract (we'll need a short MSA/PO to spin up dedicated test capacity if we move to a pilot)?
3) Any hard SLOs beyond latency and hallucination (e.g., data residency / audit log retention) we should include in the MutualActionPlan?

I'll loop Marcus in on the latency/quantization notes below. If you approve the trial, I'll send a one-page MOP and schedule the kickoff.

Thanks —
Vanessa Ortiz
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference

Hi Daniel — looping in a bit more detail on the test-suite and an initial recommendation on parity thresholds.

Hallucination test-suite (what we'll run)- A 1200-case focused set derived from your transcripts: masked-known-answers (factual retrieval), adversarial prompts (contradictory context), and synthetic numeric edge-cases (currencies, commas, negative amounts).
- Measurement: we run automatic consistency checks plus a 200-case human review sample (annotators mark hallucination = yes/no).
- Output: per-model hallucination rate (percent), and a severity-weighted score for user-facing responses.

Parity recommendation (pragmatic)
- Intent classification: parity if micro-F1 within -0.02 of baseline (i.e., no more than 2 percentage points below).
- Entity extraction: require parity or better on precision; allowing up to -0.03 on recall if compensated by higher precision.
- Answer-generation (customer-facing): require strictly lower hallucination rate than baseline OR match hallucination and at least a 5% improvement on clarity scores in human review.
- Latency: parity if 95th percentile latency is within +75ms of baseline under the trial's batching profile; if latency is significantly worse, we recommend a hybrid fallback routing for high-SLA routes.

Operational notes
- Quantized models (q4/q8) typically give the latency/cost wins but sometimes increase hallucination sensitivity. We'll include an unquantized run for comparison and flag any regression.
- For auditability: we can enable token-level logging and an immutable event stream for any trial requests that require it (adds storage/retention cost).

If Daniel and Sara confirm the dataset and procurement contact, we can spin up the trial infra this week. Vanessa — happy for you to share the MutualActionPlan draft after Sara is looped.

Marcus Lin
